text:
henry: Heads up — seeing provisioning backpressure in us-west-2 starting ~04:12 UTC. GPU warm pools failing to attach because keystore decrypts are erroring: `kms: decrypt failed: AccessDenied`. Pods stuck Pending, node kubelet spam.

sam: Can you paste the node error logs and the provisioner Describe? Also which subnets are affected, NAT vs public?

henry: Log excerpt:
```
Apr 12 04:12:35 kubelet[1234]: error: failed to fetch key from keystore: kms:Decrypt AccessDenied
Apr 12 04:12:36 provisioning-agent[76]: attach-failed: credential fetch failed, retrying
```
Nodes are in private subnets (10.40.x/24) behind NAT GW. Only GPU node pools with instance-profile "gpu-provisioner-role" failing.

henry: Noticed a firewall rule change rolled at 04:05 that tightened egress to only corporate CIDR. Terraform diff snippet: 
```
-  aws_security_group_rule.egress 0.0.0.0/0 -> 10.1.0.0/16
+  aws_security_group_rule.egress 10.1.0.0/16
```
This would block access to KMS public endpoints and S3 artifacts used during warmup.

maria: We rotated keystore keys at 04:10 (scheduled), and updated key policy to restrict decrypt to `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/provisioner` but I think the provisioner role in this account uses a federation/assume-role flow that maps to `arn:aws:sts::210987654321:assumed-role/*` — I pushed a tighter policy that inadvertently blocked cross-account decrypts. Investigating rollback.

sam: Two-pronged mitigation: 1) temporarily open egress from the private GPU subnets to KMS S3 endpoints (or add AWS managed prefix-list for KMS endpoints) 2) if IAM rollback will take time, put GPU warmups onto a non-private pool (public subnets) to speed restore. Commands to open NACL quickly:
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
```
Or better: add prefix-list for `pl-aws-kms-us-west-2` if we have one.

henry: I'm going to add an emergency egress rule to the GPU subnet SG and scale the warm-pool down/up to force retries. Doing `kubectl scale deploy/gpu-provisioner --replicas=0 && sleep 15 && kubectl scale deploy/gpu-provisioner --replicas=3` now. :crossed_fingers:

infra-bot: firewall-change: rule added by henry to sg-0abc (egress tcp/443 -> 52.94.0.0/16) at 04:22 UTC

henry: After the rule change, keystore decrypt errors stop on a couple nodes. Warm-pool started filling again, Pending -> Running.

deploy-bot: keystore rotation status: rotation applied at 04:10; current key alias has restrictions. No automatic rollback executed.

maria: I reverted the restrictive key-policy to allow the provisioner role and added a short-lived policy exception for the cross-account principal. Also enabling KMS CloudTrail log lookups for decrypt failures (will surface in 10-15m). We should also add a metric alert on `kms.decrypt_errors` for >5/min.

sam: Please add a runbook step: if warm-pool failures happen after key ops, first check (1) KMS key policy changes (2) SG egress to KMS and S3 (3) instance profile trust mapping. Quick temporary mitigations: open SG egress to KMS prefix-list, or move warm-pool to public subnet.

maria: Agreed. I'll file the postmortem and tag security+infra. Also note: the fallback to the dedicated on-demand GPUs (we routed some jobs) caused an estimated cost blip ~ $3k over the 40m outage window — include cost impact in postmortem.

henry: Filing a short postmortem now, will include timeline, terraform change id, key-policy diff, and remediation steps. Thanks for the quick assist. :thumbsup:

sam: Great — follow-up actions: revert Terraform change to intended egress (open to AWS services prefix-lists), add automated pre-checks for key-policy diffs that would deny decrypt to known roles, and add synthetic warmup checks post-key-rotation. I'll open tickets.

maria: I'll create the KMS alert and add the audit log query to the runbook. We'll also add a canary in us-west-2 private GPU pool for future rotations.

henry: Confirmed last node back to Ready at 04:38 UTC. Closing thread but keep on-call looped.
